parsed.rationale: Although both `PlaybackController` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` live in the same package (`Playback`) and share a handful of members (`installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`, `play:`, `stop:`), the structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline found no statistically significant overlap. More importantly, the two protocols encode distinct domain responsibilities: `PlaybackController` models high-level playback control with `PlaybackReason`-parameterised `play`/`stop`/`toggle`, `PlaybackState`, and a loading indicator (`isLoading:Bool`), while `TimeShiftablePlayer` models a lower-level, time-shiftable audio player with DVR semantics (`seek:`, `seekToLive:`, `secondsBehindLive:`, `maxLookbackSeconds:`, `isAtLiveEdge:Bool`, `stateStream`, `timePositionStream`, `eventStream`). Introducing a parent protocol would force an artificial coupling between two intentionally separate abstraction layers, and the differing signatures for `play` (`(reason: PlaybackReason) throws` vs `()`) and `stop` (`(reason: PlaybackReason)` vs `()`) confirm the shared names are not semantically equivalent.
